newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: ADB mulls $250 mln loan to help Pakistan markets. [CORRECTED 15:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ADB mulls $250 mln loan to help Pakistan markets. [CORRECTED 15:35 GMT]

text.p: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is considering a $250 million loan to Pakistan for developing the country's capital markets, ADB officials said on Wednesday.
S.B. Chua, ADB resident representative in Pakistan, told reporters the loan was expected to be approved by the bank's board before the end of 1997 (corrects from 1998).
"The government (of Pakistan) has adopted a Capital Market Development Programme (CMDP) with support of the Asian Development Bank," an ADB statement said.
"The CMDP is to be supported by a loan of $250 million and a package of technical assistance programme of $7.4 million."

ADB officials said the programme aimed to create a level playing field to enhance competition among market participants by easing investment requirements for the insurance industry and private sector provident funds.
It would also rationalise the tax system for private corporate income securities and mutual funds.

A securities and exchange commission is also to be set up under the programme to oversee the regulation of securities market and the state Corporate Law Authority to be restructured so it could better focus on corporate affairs.
The programme also envisages the setting up of an autonomous insurance regulatory authority to replace the existing office of Controller of Insurance.

Chua said the loan would be disbursed in two equal tranches in two years to support Pakistan's efforts for capital market development, partially compensate for revenue loss due to taxation changes and set up a regulatory infrastructure.
"Some of the reforms the government has to implement have a cost attached," said Shamshad Akhtar, a senior ADB economist leading an appraisal mission to Pakistan to discuss CDMP.
She said that after two weeks of consultations with government officials and private sector, she felt the time was ripe to undertake development of capital markets in Pakistan.
Akhtar said the programme should increase domestic and foreign flows in Pakistan, raise investor confidence, bring more liquidity, and efficiency and speed in transactions.
Antonio Quila, Manila-based manager of ADB's financial sector and industry division, said it was important for countries now to develop their capital markets to be able to raise domestic resources.

"The CMDP supports modernisation of securities market infrastructure and its linkages through automation of all the stock exchanges and centralised trading, clearing, settlement and depository systems," the statement said.

"The key market participants are also exploring the possibility for establishing an over-the-counter market to allow for the development of orderly and electronic screen-based secondary trading in debt instruments," it added.
